title: image-compat-canary-harden-rollforward-playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement: Upgrading CUDA/drivers and container base images causes intermittent regressions for a subset of models (memory fragmentation, kernel fallback, occasional OOMs) which only surface under production-like batching and long token sequences. We need an operationalized canary and honeypot matrix that validates new images, SBOMs and driver stacks against representative workloads before rollout to LTS channels. This ticket defines the playbook, automation, and gating signals for image compatibility canaries and automated rollforward/rollback policies. Goals: 1) Define a small but representative matrix of hardware+driver+image variants to run on every image/artifact build. 2) Build automated canary runs that exercise: short/long sequence generation, KV cache warmups, continuous batching, and stress burst traffic. 3) Surface deterministic regression signals (increased median latency, kv-cache miss rate, kernel-fallback counts, GPU OOMs, token generation divergence) into a release gate. 4) Automate artifact promotion to LTS or pinset updates only when gates pass; allow fast rollforward with immutable build promotion if rollback required. 5) Keep SBOM and artifact provenance linked to canary runs for audit and incident debug. Scope: Canary job definitions in CI and a parallel 'honeypot' nightly cluster that mirrors production autoscaling and batch shapes. Tagging and metadata pipelines to attach SBOMs, driver pins, kernel logs, and perf snapshots to each build. A rollout gate evaluator (service) that aggregates the signals and recommends: pass, fail, or manual-review. Playbook and runbook for engineers and SREs to follow on failures (triage, rollback, mitigation steps). Out-of-scope: full LTS release planning; we focus on pre-promotion validation and automated gating for artifact promotion.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary matrix runs are configured and green for 90% of daily builds; failures produce a triage ticket automatically. 2) At least four deterministic signals (latency regression, kernel-fallback count, KV-cache miss delta, GPU OOM rate) are computed per run and surfaced to the gate evaluator. 3) Successful image builds are automatically annotated with SBOM link, driver pinset, and a promotion tag 'candidate-lts' when gate passes. 4) Rollforward automation can promote a new image to canary fleet within 10 minutes of an approved run. 5) Documentation and a playbook exist in Confluence with troubleshooting checklists and required on-call notifications.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 0-2): prototype matrix and single-node canary jobs in CI for three model families (chat, long-ctx, embeddings). Phase 2 (week 3-6): deploy honeypot nightly cluster with production-like batch shapes and autorun across three driver versions. Phase 3 (week 7-9): integrate gate evaluator to the artifact promotion pipeline and run a pilot image promotion to 'candidate-lts'. Phase 4 (week 10): full LTS candidate validation and handoff to release managers. Gating policy: automatic PASS if key signals within threshold band; FAIL if any critical signal (GPU OOM, >30% kernel-fallback increase) triggers; MANUAL-REVIEW for borderline regressions with >10% P50 latency increase or divergence on quality evals. Canary targeting rules: start at 2 nodes per region for low-risk, expand to 10 nodes when pilot green.
